questions.question: How would you read a decimal number safely without the program crashing if the user types text?
explanations: nextDouble() throws InputMismatchException if the input is not a number.
Correct. hasNextDouble() checks before reading, avoiding exceptions.
try-catch works but hasNextXxx() is the idiomatic way with Scanner.
Integer.parseInt() is for strings, not for console input.

questions.question: What is the difference between `next()` and `nextLine()`?
options: next() reads one word, nextLine() reads the whole line
next() reads a line, nextLine() reads a word
next() is for integers, nextLine() for text
explanations: Correct. next() reads up to the first whitespace. nextLine() reads up to the end of the line.
It is the other way around.
Both read text; nextInt() is for integers.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to close Scanner with `sc.close()`?
options: So the program does not crash
explanations: The program does not crash without close(), but it is bad practice.
Correct. close() releases the underlying System.in resource and prevents memory leaks.
It is not strictly mandatory, but it is good practice.
It does not erase data; it releases system resources.
